items.name: theme
items.title: Theme
items.description: The tokens every Rivier UI component draws from: colours, the highlight colour, roundness, motion. Light and dark.

meta.when: Always: install it first and import it after Tailwind in the global stylesheet.

items.name: announce
items.title: Announce
items.description: Says a message to screen-reader users through one shared live region, politely or at once, without moving focus.

meta.when: Something changed that a sighted person can see but no focus change will read out: an item was moved, a filter applied, a total changed, a reply finished. Not for content the person is about to read anyway, and not for errors on a field (use the field's own message). A component that is already a live region (status-line, toaster) does not need it.
meta.example:
announce("Lunch moved to position 2 of 5");
announce("The connection was lost", "assertive");

items.name: cn
items.title: Cn
items.description: Joins class names and resolves Tailwind conflicts, so a class passed in wins over a component's own.

meta.when: Every component uses it. Use it wherever classes are combined conditionally.
meta.example: cn("px-4 py-2", isActive && "bg-primary", className)

items.name: direction
items.title: Direction
items.description: Tells whether an element reads right to left, and turns "start" and "end" arrow keys and offsets the right way round for it.

meta.when: A component handles Left and Right arrow keys, or moves something sideways with a transform, and must work in right-to-left pages. Layout itself needs no code: use logical utilities (ps-, ms-, start-, text-start). To set a direction for part of a page use direction-provider.

items.name: motion
items.title: Motion
items.description: The motion tokens as numbers for the motion package (easing, durations, a pointer spring), the useMotionSafe gate, and the entrance engine the reveal components share.

meta.when: Any component animated with the motion package: take timing from here so it matches the CSS tokens, and gate on useMotionSafe so server markup is the final state. For CSS transitions use the duration-* and ease-out utilities instead.

items.name: theme-color
items.title: Theme Color
items.description: Resolves a theme CSS variable such as "--highlight" to an rgb() string that three.js and canvas code can parse, and re-reads it when the theme changes.

meta.when: Anything that cannot use a Tailwind class or `var()`: three.js materials, canvas drawing. In markup use the token classes (`bg-primary`, `fill-chart-1`) instead.

items.name: use-controllable-state
items.title: Use Controllable State
items.description: State that a parent may control: it follows `value` when one is given and keeps its own from `defaultValue` when not, calling `onChange` either way.

meta.when: Writing a component that should work both controlled (`value` + `onValueChange`) and uncontrolled (`defaultValue`), which every input-like component in the library does. Radix primitives already do this for their own state; use this for state the library adds on top.

items.name: use-media
items.title: Use Media
items.description: Follows an audio or video element (playing, time, duration, buffered, volume, rate, text tracks, waiting, error) as React state, with the actions to drive it, the context player parts share, and time formatting through Intl.

meta.when: Building player parts around a `<video>` or `<audio>` element the project renders. video-player, audio-player, captions and scene-strip are built on it; use it directly for a control they do not have. The element stays the source of truth: sources, HLS and DRM are attached to it by the project, and nothing here loads or decodes media.

items.name: use-size
items.title: Use Size
items.description: Measures an element with ResizeObserver and returns its content width and height in whole pixels.

meta.when: Drawing to the size of a container: charts, canvases. For layout that only needs to adapt, use container queries (`@container`, `@md:`) instead.
meta.example:
const { ref, width, height } = useSize(); return
{width > 0 && }
;

items.name: accordion
items.title: Accordion
items.description: Stacked sections whose content opens and closes under its heading.

meta.when: Questions and answers, or long settings where people need a few sections out of many. `type="single"` keeps one open (add `collapsible` so it can be closed again); `type="multiple"` lets several be open. For views that replace each other in one place use tabs. Do not hide content everyone needs.
meta.example:
<Accordion type="single" collapsible defaultValue="shipping">
  <AccordionItem value="shipping">
    <AccordionTrigger>How long does delivery take?</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>Two to four working days.</AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem value="returns">
    <AccordionTrigger>Can I send it back?</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>Yes, within thirty days.</AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>

items.name: alert
items.title: Alert
items.description: A message in the page with an icon, a title, a description and an optional action. Four variants: info, success, warning, destructive.

meta.when: Telling the reader something about the page or the result of an action, in place. For a message that appears and leaves use a toast; for one that needs an answer use a dialog.
meta.example:
<Alert variant="success">
  <AlertTitle>Payment received</AlertTitle>
  <AlertDescription>A receipt is on its way to your inbox.</AlertDescription>
</Alert>
<Alert variant="destructive">
  <AlertTitle>The card was declined</AlertTitle>
  <AlertDescription>Check the number and the expiry date, then try again.</AlertDescription>
  <AlertAction><Button size="sm" variant="outline">Try again</Button></AlertAction>
</Alert>

items.name: audio-player
items.title: Audio Player
items.description: The parts of a sound player around an `<audio>` element: play, a waveform that is also the time bar, time, speed and mute.

meta.when: A voice note, a recording, a clip of music or narration a person plays and seeks in. The project gives the element its source and, for the waveform, the peaks (computed ahead of time, or with computePeaks for a short clip); without peaks the bar is a flat line of the same size. Offer a Transcript (from captions) for anything spoken. Nothing plays by itself. For video use video-player; for a plain time bar without a waveform use scrubber.
meta.example:
<AudioPlayer aria-label="Voice note from Ana">
  <AudioPlayerAudio src="/note.mp3" />
  <AudioPlayerPlay />
  <AudioPlayerWaveform peaks={peaks} />
  <AudioPlayerTime />
  <AudioPlayerRate />
  <AudioPlayerMute />
</AudioPlayer>

// Peaks for a short clip, in the browser
const peaks = await computePeaks(await (await fetch("/note.mp3")).arrayBuffer(), 64);

items.name: avatar
items.title: Avatar
items.description: A round picture of a person or a team, with initials shown until the image loads or when it fails, and a group that overlaps.

meta.when: Showing who something belongs to. Always give AvatarFallback initials; give AvatarImage an alt (the name), or alt="" when the name is printed next to it.
meta.example:
<Avatar size="lg">
  <AvatarImage src="/people/hana.jpg" alt="Hana Ito" />
  <AvatarFallback>HI</AvatarFallback>
</Avatar>
<AvatarGroup aria-label="Team">
  <Avatar><AvatarFallback>AK</AvatarFallback></Avatar>
  <Avatar><AvatarFallback>BL</AvatarFallback></Avatar>
  <Avatar><AvatarFallback>+3</AvatarFallback></Avatar>
</AvatarGroup>

items.name: badge
items.title: Badge
items.description: A small label for a status, a count or a category. Six variants and an optional leading dot.

meta.when: Marking a state or a tag next to other content. It is not clickable: for a removable or selectable chip use a button with size "sm".
meta.example:
<Badge>New</Badge>
<Badge variant="soft">Beta</Badge>
<Badge variant="success" dot>Live</Badge>
<Badge variant="outline">Draft</Badge>

items.name: bottom-sheet
items.title: Bottom Sheet
items.description: A panel that rises from the bottom edge, rests at one of several heights (snap points), and can be dragged between them or down to dismiss, with a keyboard handle that does the same.

meta.when: Phones first: details, filters, a picker or a secondary task that should stay within reach of the thumb and may be peeked at before it is opened fully. With `modal={false}` it stays open while the page behind is used (a player, a route summary). For a panel from a side edge, or one with no snap points on a desktop, use sheet; for a short decision use dialog; beside the content on wide screens use dock. Always give it a BottomSheetTitle (add className="sr-only" to hide it). Opened by state with no BottomSheetTrigger, focus does not return on close: refocus the opener in `onCloseAutoFocus` on BottomSheetContent.
meta.example:
<BottomSheet snapPoints={[0.4, 0.9]}>
  <BottomSheetTrigger asChild><Button variant="outline">Details</Button></BottomSheetTrigger>
  <BottomSheetContent>
    <BottomSheetHandle />
    <BottomSheetHeader>
      <BottomSheetTitle>Saturday</BottomSheetTitle>
      <BottomSheetDescription>Three things planned.</BottomSheetDescription>
    </BottomSheetHeader>
    <BottomSheetBody>…</BottomSheetBody>
    <BottomSheetFooter>
      <BottomSheetClose asChild><Button>Done</Button></BottomSheetClose>
    </BottomSheetFooter>
  </BottomSheetContent>
</BottomSheet>

// Controlled, in pixels and rems, staying open while the page is used
<BottomSheet open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} snapPoints={["6rem", "320px", 1]} snap={snap} onSnapChange={setSnap} modal={false} dismissible={false}>
  …
</BottomSheet>

items.name: breadcrumb
items.title: Breadcrumb
items.description: The path from the top of the site to the current page, as links with separators.

meta.when: Pages nested three or more levels deep, above the page title. The last item is the current page: a BreadcrumbPage, not a link. For moving between sibling pages use tabs or the navbar. With a router link, pass it through `asChild`.
meta.example:
<Breadcrumb>
  <BreadcrumbList>
    <BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbLink href="/">Home</BreadcrumbLink></BreadcrumbItem>
    <BreadcrumbSeparator />
    <BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbLink href="/projects">Projects</BreadcrumbLink></BreadcrumbItem>
    <BreadcrumbSeparator />
    <BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbPage>Atlas</BreadcrumbPage></BreadcrumbItem>
  </BreadcrumbList>
</Breadcrumb>

items.name: button
items.title: Button
items.description: A button, or a link that looks like one. Five variants, three sizes, a loading state.

meta.when: Any action. One "solid" per view for the main action; "outline" or "ghost" for the rest; "destructive" only for deleting.

items.name: calendar
items.title: Calendar
items.description: A month grid for choosing a day, several days or a range of days, with days that can be unavailable for a stated reason and days that carry a mark. Days are plain "YYYY-MM-DD" strings, so no time zone can move them.

meta.when: Choosing dates where seeing the month matters: a booking, a stay, a deadline. It stays on the page; to open it from a field use date-picker. Never use the browser's native date input beside it. For a date far in the past that the person knows by heart (a birthday) three plain fields are quicker. Pass `locale` (the page's language) so that names, numerals and the first day of the week are right; without it the calendar is in English.

items.name: captions
items.title: Captions
items.description: Captions drawn by the page instead of the browser, on a solid ground that reads on any picture, and a transcript: every line of a clip as a list that can be pressed to go there.

meta.when: Inside video-player (Captions sits above the controls and moves with them) or beside audio-player (Transcript, or Captions with `inline`). Captions are for people who cannot hear the sound; a Transcript is also the alternative for people who cannot see or play it, so offer one for anything spoken. The lines come from a caption track of the media element (`<track kind="captions">`), or from `cues` the project passes. Not a live region: with the sound on, a screen reader would talk over it.
meta.example:
// In a video player: the lines of the element's caption track
<VideoPlayer aria-label="Loading the kiln" defaultCaptions>
  <VideoPlayerVideo src="/kiln.mp4"><track kind="captions" src="/kiln.en.vtt" srcLang="en" label="English" /></VideoPlayerVideo>
  <Captions />
  <VideoPlayerControls>…</VideoPlayerControls>
</VideoPlayer>

// Beside an audio player: cues from the project, as a transcript
const cues = [{ start: 0, end: 4, text: "Welcome." }, { start: 4, end: 9, text: "This is the yard." }];
<AudioPlayer aria-label="A walk through the yard">
  <AudioPlayerAudio src="/yard.mp3" />
  <AudioPlayerPlay /> <AudioPlayerWaveform peaks={peaks} />
  <Transcript cues={cues} aria-label="Transcript" lang="en" />
</AudioPlayer>

items.name: card
items.title: Card
items.description: A flat surface with a hairline edge, and parts for a header, title, description, content and footer.

meta.when: Grouping related content: a plan, a stat, a form section. For a grid of unequal cards use bento-grid.
meta.example:
<Card>
  <CardHeader>
    <CardTitle>Usage</CardTitle>
    <CardDescription>This month</CardDescription>
  </CardHeader>
  <CardContent>1,204 requests</CardContent>
  <CardFooter><Button size="sm">Details</Button></CardFooter>
</Card>

items.name: carousel
items.title: Carousel
items.description: A row of slides that is scrolled sideways one at a time (or a few at a time), with previous and next buttons, dots or a count, keys, and an optional autoplay that always has a pause button.

meta.when: A handful of pictures or cards of equal weight where one (or a few) is enough at a time: the photos of a place, featured items, quotes. It is the browser's own scrolling with CSS scroll snap, so a swipe, a trackpad and momentum work as they do everywhere, right-to-left pages mirror by themselves and nothing moves under reduced motion; no carousel package is used (Embla, MIT, moves slides with transforms on its own engine, which this does not need). Set how many slides show with a basis on the slides (`className="basis-1/2 md:basis-1/3"`). Do not hide content a person must read in a carousel, and do not autoplay anything with text to read. For looking at pictures large use gallery with lightbox; for scenes of a clip use scene-strip; for thousands of items use virtual-list.
meta.example:

// Controlled, three to a view on wide screens, with a count; and one that plays by itself {cards.map((card) => …)} …

items.name: certainty-legend
items.title: Certainty Legend
items.description: A small key of three or four named classes (how sure something is, or any other kind), each with its own pattern as well as its own colour, where each class can be switched off and on.

meta.when: A scene, a map, a drawing or a chart marks its parts by class and the reader needs the key and a way to hide a class: what is recorded, what is worked out, what is a guess. The project supplies the names; the legend reports which classes are shown (`onValueChange`) and the project applies that to its own scene. Use CertaintySwatch to draw the same pattern in the scene's own key or in a caption. The pattern is what tells classes apart for someone who cannot tell the colours apart, so use it in the scene too. For filters with no key use chip; for the series of a chart, the chart's own legend.

items.name: checkbox
items.title: Checkbox
items.description: A checkbox with checked, unchecked and indeterminate states.

meta.when: Choosing any number of options, or agreeing to something that is submitted with a form. For a setting that applies at once use switch; for exactly one of several use radio-group.
meta.example:
<Label><Checkbox defaultChecked /> Email me product news</Label>
<Checkbox checked="indeterminate" aria-label="Select all rows" />

items.name: chip
items.title: Chip
items.description: A small pill for one short value: a filter that is on and can be removed, a suggestion to press, or one of a set of choices that can be switched on and off.

meta.when: Filters in effect above a list (Chip with ChipRemove), suggested replies or refinements under a message or a search (ChipButton), and choosing one or several short options such as moods, tags or times of day (ChipGroup). For a status that cannot be pressed use badge; for two to five views of the same thing use segmented-control; for long labels use checkboxes or radio-group.

items.name: combobox
items.title: Combobox
items.description: A select with a search field: a button that shows the choice and opens a list that narrows as one types.

meta.when: Choosing one value from a list too long to scan: a country, a city, a person, a product. Under about eight options use select (or radio-group, or segmented-control for two to five); for running actions rather than choosing a value use command; for several values use chip or checkboxes. Name the trigger with a Label (`htmlFor` its `id`) or `aria-label`. Each item's `value` is what is stored; what is typed is matched against the item's text.
meta.example:
const CITIES = [{ value: "lis", label: "Lisbon" }, { value: "opo", label: "Porto" }];
const [city, setCity] = useState("");

<Combobox value={city} onValueChange={setCity} name="city">
  <ComboboxTrigger aria-label="City" className="w-56">
    <ComboboxValue placeholder="Choose a city">{CITIES.find((item) => item.value === city)?.label}</ComboboxValue>
  </ComboboxTrigger>
  <ComboboxContent aria-label="Cities">
    <ComboboxInput placeholder="Search cities" />
    <ComboboxList>
      <ComboboxEmpty>No city found.</ComboboxEmpty>
      {CITIES.map((item) => (
        <ComboboxItem key={item.value} value={item.value}>{item.label}</ComboboxItem>
      ))}
    </ComboboxList>
  </ComboboxContent>
</Combobox>

items.name: command
items.title: Command
items.description: A command palette: a search field over a filtered, keyboard-driven list of actions, inline or in a dialog.

meta.when: Fast access to many actions or pages by typing (the Ctrl/Cmd+K palette), or a searchable list inside a popover. For a handful of actions use dropdown-menu. CommandDialog is usually opened by a shortcut, with no trigger, so focus has nowhere to return: remember the opener (`opener.current = document.activeElement` before opening) and refocus it in `onCloseAutoFocus={(event) => { event.preventDefault(); opener.current?.focus(); }}`.
meta.example:
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

<Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Search</Button>
<CommandDialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <CommandInput placeholder="Type a command" />
  <CommandList>
    <CommandEmpty>Nothing found.</CommandEmpty>
    <CommandGroup heading="Pages">
      <CommandItem onSelect={() => setOpen(false)}>Dashboard</CommandItem>
      <CommandItem onSelect={() => setOpen(false)}>Settings <CommandShortcut>Ctrl ,</CommandShortcut></CommandItem>
    </CommandGroup>
    <CommandSeparator />
    <CommandGroup heading="Account">
      <CommandItem onSelect={() => setOpen(false)}>Sign out</CommandItem>
    </CommandGroup>
  </CommandList>
</CommandDialog>

items.name: compare-slider
items.title: Compare Slider
items.description: Two layers of the same size, one over the other, with a divider that is dragged or moved with the keyboard to show more of one and less of the other: then and now, before and after.

meta.when: Comparing two views of the same thing in the same frame: two pictures, two maps, two 3D viewers, any two children. Each side has a visible name. The divider is a slider, so it works without dragging. The frame is drawn left to right in every language (a picture is not mirrored in a right-to-left page), so the first layer is always on the left and the arrow keys move the divider the way they point. For two things that are not the same view use two cards side by side; for many pictures use gallery or carousel.
meta.example: // Controlled, with any two children

items.name: compare-table
items.title: Compare Table
items.description: Two to four things side by side, attribute by attribute: a table whose first column (the attribute names) stays in view while the things scroll sideways inside it on narrow screens.

meta.when: Helping someone choose between a few similar things: plans, products, places, quotes. Give every thing the same rows, in the same order. For plain rows of data use table; for more than four things let people pick which to compare first; for one thing's details use a description list or card.
meta.example:
<CompareTable label="Compare the two plans" columns={2} onlyDifferences={onlyDifferences}>
  <CompareHeader corner="Plan">
    <CompareColumn><CompareColumnTitle>Starter</CompareColumnTitle><Button size="sm">Choose</Button></CompareColumn>
    <CompareColumn><CompareColumnTitle>Team</CompareColumnTitle><Button size="sm">Choose</Button></CompareColumn>
  </CompareHeader>
  <CompareGroup title="Basics">
    <CompareRow label="Price a month">
      <CompareCell value={12} best>€12</CompareCell>
      <CompareCell value={29}>€29</CompareCell>
    </CompareRow>
    <CompareRow label="Support">
      <CompareCell value="email">By email</CompareCell>
      <CompareCell value="email">By email</CompareCell>
    </CompareRow>
  </CompareGroup>
</CompareTable>

items.name: composer
items.title: Composer
items.description: The box a person writes a message in: a field that grows with the text, a list of attachments, and a toolbar with slots for an attach button, a voice button and send (which becomes stop while a reply is on its way).

meta.when: Under a thread, or anywhere a person sends free text to an assistant or to other people. It owns the text and the keys (Enter sends, Shift+Enter makes a new line, nothing is sent while an input method is composing); the project owns the files, the microphone and the sending. For one line with no attachments (a search box) use input-group; for a long form field use textarea.
meta.example:
<Composer onSubmit={send} busy={replying} onStop={stop}>
  <ComposerAttachments aria-label="Attachments">
    {files.map((file) => (
      <ComposerAttachment key={file.name} onRemove={() => remove(file)} removeLabel={`Remove ${file.name}`}>{file.name}</ComposerAttachment>
    ))}
  </ComposerAttachments>
  <ComposerInput aria-label="Message" placeholder="Ask anything" />
  <ComposerToolbar>
    <ComposerAttachButton aria-label="Attach a file" onFiles={add} accept="image/*" multiple />
    <ComposerVoiceButton pressed={listening} onPressedChange={setListening} />
    <ComposerSubmit />
  </ComposerToolbar>
</Composer>

items.name: consent
items.title: Consent
items.description: Asks permission before something is switched on or shared: what is asked for, item by item, each optional one with its own switch that starts off, and two equal buttons to allow or decline. As a sheet (ConsentSheet) or in the page (ConsentPanel).

meta.when: Before sharing a person's data with another party, connecting an account, turning on an assistant or a feature that reads their content, or using a device permission. One consent per purpose, in plain words, at the moment it is needed. Nothing is pre-ticked and declining is as easy as allowing. For a yes or no about an action the person just started (delete, leave) use dialog; for a cookie notice use the same parts in a ConsentPanel.
meta.example:
<ConsentSheet side="bottom" defaultValue={[]} onAccept={(granted) => connect(granted)} onDecline={skip} onDismiss={skip}>
  <ConsentTrigger asChild><Button>Connect calendar</Button></ConsentTrigger>
  <ConsentContent>
    <ConsentHeader>
      <ConsentTitle>Let the planner see your calendar?</ConsentTitle>
      <ConsentDescription>It is used to avoid times when you are busy. You can stop this in Settings at any time.</ConsentDescription>
    </ConsentHeader>
    <ConsentScopes>
      <ConsentScope value="busy" title="Busy times" description="When you are busy, without what the events are." required requiredLabel="Always needed" />
      <ConsentScope value="titles" title="Event names" description="So that suggestions can mention what you have planned." />
    </ConsentScopes>
    <ConsentDetails summary="How this is stored">Kept for 30 days, never sold, deleted when you disconnect.</ConsentDetails>
    <ConsentFooter>
      <ConsentDecline>Do not allow</ConsentDecline>
      <ConsentAccept>Allow</ConsentAccept>
    </ConsentFooter>
  </ConsentContent>
</ConsentSheet>

items.name: context-menu
items.title: Context Menu
items.description: A menu of actions that opens at the pointer on right-click, and on a long press on touch screens: items, checkbox and radio items, labels, separators, sub-menus and a shortcut slot.

meta.when: Shortcuts to actions on a thing in a dense interface (a file, a row, a canvas object). Nothing shows that it exists, so every action in it must also be reachable another way; for a visible button use dropdown-menu.
meta.example:
<ContextMenu>
  <ContextMenuTrigger className="flex h-32 items-center justify-center rounded-surface border border-dashed text-sm">
    Right-click, or press and hold
  </ContextMenuTrigger>
  <ContextMenuContent>
    <ContextMenuItem>Open <ContextMenuShortcut>Enter</ContextMenuShortcut></ContextMenuItem>
    <ContextMenuCheckboxItem checked>Pinned</ContextMenuCheckboxItem>
    <ContextMenuSub>
      <ContextMenuSubTrigger>Label</ContextMenuSubTrigger>
      <ContextMenuSubContent>
        <ContextMenuRadioGroup value="none">
          <ContextMenuRadioItem value="none">None</ContextMenuRadioItem>
          <ContextMenuRadioItem value="urgent">Urgent</ContextMenuRadioItem>
        </ContextMenuRadioGroup>
      </ContextMenuSubContent>
    </ContextMenuSub>
    <ContextMenuSeparator />
    <ContextMenuItem variant="destructive">Delete</ContextMenuItem>
  </ContextMenuContent>
</ContextMenu>

items.name: countdown
items.title: Countdown
items.description: The time left until a moment, as text that counts down ("4 min 12 s"), announced to screen-reader users only at the moments the project lists.

meta.when: Something the person holds for a limited time: a reserved seat, a price that is kept, a code that expires, a session about to end. Say what happens at the end and offer a way to get more time beside it. Not for decoration or pressure: a countdown that restarts or means nothing is a dark pattern. For progress through a known amount of work use progress.
meta.example: Your seats are held for{" "} `${left} left to finish booking`} onExpire={release} expiredLabel="no longer: the hold has ended" />

items.name: date-picker
items.title: Date Picker
items.description: A button that shows a date, or a range of dates, and opens a calendar in a popover to choose it. Values are "YYYY-MM-DD" strings.

meta.when: A date or a stay inside a form or a toolbar, where a calendar that is always open would take too much room. When the calendar is the main thing on the screen use calendar itself. Never the browser's native date input. Name the button by passing `aria-labelledby` with the id of its visible label: the chosen date is added to the name.
meta.example:

items.name: dialog
items.title: Dialog
items.description: A modal window over a dimmed page, with parts for a header, title, description and footer.

meta.when: A short task or a decision that must be finished or dismissed before going on. For a panel from an edge (menus, filters, details) use sheet; for something small attached to a control use popover. Always give it a DialogTitle (add className="sr-only" to hide it). Opened by a DialogTrigger, focus returns to that trigger on close. Opened by state with no trigger (a shortcut, a menu item), Radix has nothing to return to: remember the opener (`opener.current = document.activeElement` before opening) and refocus it in `onCloseAutoFocus={(event) => { event.preventDefault(); opener.current?.focus(); }}` on DialogContent.
meta.example:
<Dialog>
  <DialogTrigger asChild><Button variant="outline">Rename</Button></DialogTrigger>
  <DialogContent>
    <DialogHeader>
      <DialogTitle>Rename project</DialogTitle>
      <DialogDescription>The address of the project does not change.</DialogDescription>
    </DialogHeader>
    <input aria-label="Name" defaultValue="Atlas" className="h-control rounded-control border border-input px-3 text-base" />
    <DialogFooter>
      <DialogClose asChild><Button variant="outline">Cancel</Button></DialogClose>
      <Button>Save</Button>
    </DialogFooter>
  </DialogContent>
</Dialog>

items.name: direction-provider
items.title: Direction Provider
items.description: Sets the reading direction (left to right, or right to left) for everything inside it: the `dir` attribute for layout and text, and the context Radix-based components read for arrow keys and placement.

meta.when: Once around the app, with the direction of the current language, in any product that has or may get a right-to-left language (Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, Urdu, Dhivehi). Also around one part of a page in the other direction. A product in one left-to-right language does not need it. Put `dir` on <html> as well (the provider's own element covers only what is inside it; menus and dialogs are portalled to <body>). For people's own words in an unknown language use `dir="auto"` on that element instead.

items.name: dock
items.title: Dock
items.description: A layout of main content with a panel docked beside it that stays while the person works: the panel can be resized with a splitter, collapsed to a slim bar, and on narrow containers gives way to a bar at the bottom.

meta.when: A working surface that belongs beside the content and is not modal: a plan next to a conversation, an inspector next to a canvas, details next to a list. For a panel that covers the page for a moment use sheet; for two fixed columns with no resizing use split. Write the parts in reading order: DockMain, DockResizer, DockPanel for a panel at the end; DockPanel, DockResizer, DockMain with side="start". Below 42rem of its own width (another width with `stackBelow`) the panel and splitter are hidden and DockBar shows at the bottom: open the panel's content in a bottom-sheet from `onOpenStacked`. Where the content ends in a region that must stay lowest (a composer), put a second DockBar inside DockMain above that region with `show="stacked"`, and give the one after the panel `show="collapsed"`. Give the Dock a height (it fills its parent).
meta.example:
…the conversation… …the plan… setSheetOpen(true)}>Plan · 3 stops // Controlled, in pixels, at the start … // Stacks below 56rem; on a narrow dock the bar sits above the composer, not under it
…the conversation…
setSheetOpen(true)}>Plan · 3 stops
…the composer…
 … Plan · 3 stops

items.name: dropdown-menu
items.title: Dropdown Menu
items.description: A menu of actions that opens from a button: items, checkbox and radio items, labels, separators, sub-menus and a shortcut slot.

meta.when: A list of actions or options behind one button (an account menu, "more" on a row). For choosing one value in a form use select; for actions on right-click use context-menu; for free content use popover. An icon-only trigger needs an `aria-label`.
meta.example:
<DropdownMenu>
  <DropdownMenuTrigger asChild><Button variant="outline">Options</Button></DropdownMenuTrigger>
  <DropdownMenuContent align="start">
    <DropdownMenuLabel>Project</DropdownMenuLabel>
    <DropdownMenuItem>Rename <DropdownMenuShortcut>F2</DropdownMenuShortcut></DropdownMenuItem>
    <DropdownMenuCheckboxItem checked>Show in sidebar</DropdownMenuCheckboxItem>
    <DropdownMenuSub>
      <DropdownMenuSubTrigger>Move to</DropdownMenuSubTrigger>
      <DropdownMenuSubContent>
        <DropdownMenuRadioGroup value="work">
          <DropdownMenuRadioItem value="work">Work</DropdownMenuRadioItem>
          <DropdownMenuRadioItem value="archive">Archive</DropdownMenuRadioItem>
        </DropdownMenuRadioGroup>
      </DropdownMenuSubContent>
    </DropdownMenuSub>
    <DropdownMenuSeparator />
    <DropdownMenuItem variant="destructive">Delete</DropdownMenuItem>
  </DropdownMenuContent>
</DropdownMenu>

items.name: dropzone
items.title: Dropzone
items.description: A place to choose files to upload, by dropping them, pasting them or pressing a button, and the rows that show each file's progress with slots for pause, resume, retry and remove.

meta.when: Adding pictures, documents or other files where progress matters: a listing's photos, attachments, an import. It contains no upload engine: the project uploads (plain, or resumable such as tus) and tells each row its state and progress. For one small file in a form, an input with type="file" is enough. Name the dropzone with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, and word rejected files yourself from the reason given to `onReject`.
meta.example:
<Dropzone accept="image/*" maxSize={10_000_000} onFiles={start} onReject={explain} aria-label="Add pictures">
  <DropzoneHint>Drop pictures here, or</DropzoneHint>
  <DropzoneButton>Choose pictures</DropzoneButton>
</Dropzone>
<UploadList aria-label="Pictures being added">
  {uploads.map((upload) => (
    <UploadItem key={upload.id} name={upload.file.name} size={upload.file.size} state={upload.state}>
      <UploadProgress value={upload.percent} />
      <UploadActions>
        {upload.state === "uploading" ? <UploadPause onClick={() => pause(upload.id)} /> : null}
        {upload.state === "paused" ? <UploadResume onClick={() => resume(upload.id)} /> : null}
        {upload.state === "failed" ? <UploadRetry onClick={() => retry(upload.id)} /> : null}
        <UploadRemove onClick={() => remove(upload.id)} />
      </UploadActions>
    </UploadItem>
  ))}
</UploadList>

// A state of the project's own, with its word and tone; and a row that is not a list item
<UploadItem as="div" name="walk.mp4" state="checking" stateLabel="Being checked" stateTone="warning" />

items.name: empty-state
items.title: Empty State
items.description: What a list, a table or a search shows when there is nothing in it: an icon, a title, a description and an action.

meta.when: An empty list, zero search results, a first run. Say what belongs here and offer the one action that fills it. For a failure use alert; while loading use skeleton.
meta.example:
<EmptyState
  title="No projects yet"
  description="Projects you create will appear here."
  action={<Button>New project</Button>}
/>
<EmptyState icon={<SearchX />} title="No results" description="Try a shorter search." bordered={false} />

items.name: fact-row
items.title: Fact Row
items.description: One thing the system knows or remembers about a person or a record, shown with where it came from and what the person can do about it: correct it in place, say it is no longer true, or have it removed.

meta.when: Showing people what is held about them and letting them control it: remembered preferences, profile details filled in by an assistant, imported data, settings inferred from use. Every fact gets a source and at least one action. The words of the actions are the project's (the component names none). For plain label and value pairs nobody can change use a description list; for a form use field.
meta.example:
<FactList aria-label="What we remember">
  <FactRow removed={forgotten} removedMessage="Diet was forgotten" restoredMessage="Diet was restored">
    <FactLabel>Diet</FactLabel>
    <FactValue>{diet}</FactValue>
    <FactSource>
      <SourceChip icon={<MessageSquare />}>You said this on 3 May</SourceChip>
    </FactSource>
    <FactActions aria-label="Diet">
      <FactEditTrigger>Edit</FactEditTrigger>
      <FactAction onClick={endDiet}>Not true any more</FactAction>
      <FactAction onClick={() => setForgotten(true)}>Forget this</FactAction>
    </FactActions>
    <FactEditor aria-label="Diet" defaultValue={diet} onSave={setDiet} savedMessage="Diet was changed" />
    <FactRemoved>
      Diet was forgotten. <FactUndo onClick={() => setForgotten(false)}>Undo</FactUndo>
    </FactRemoved>
  </FactRow>
</FactList>

items.name: field
items.title: Field
items.description: Lays out a label, a control, a description and an error message, and connects them (htmlFor, id, aria-describedby, aria-invalid) without hand-written ids.

meta.when: Every control in a form. Put the control inside FieldControl; render FieldError only when there is a message and the field turns invalid by itself. Use orientation="horizontal" for a checkbox or switch beside its label, and FieldControl group for a radio group, toggle group or slider.
meta.example:
<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Email</FieldLabel>
  <FieldControl><Input type="email" /></FieldControl>
  <FieldDescription>We only use it to reply.</FieldDescription>
  <FieldError>{error}</FieldError>
</Field>
<Field orientation="horizontal">
  <FieldControl><Switch /></FieldControl>
  <FieldLabel>Weekly summary</FieldLabel>
</Field>
<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Plan</FieldLabel>
  <FieldControl group>
    <RadioGroup defaultValue="pro">
      <Label><RadioGroupItem value="free" /> Free</Label>
      <Label><RadioGroupItem value="pro" /> Pro</Label>
    </RadioGroup>
  </FieldControl>
</Field>

items.name: gallery
items.title: Gallery
items.description: A set of picture tiles that open a full-screen viewer: a mosaic of one large and several small, an even grid, or a row that scrolls sideways.

meta.when: Showing several pictures of one thing where each can be looked at closely: a place, a product, a piece of work. GalleryLightbox takes a list of pictures and does everything; Gallery, GalleryItem and GalleryImage are the parts, to put inside your own Lightbox or to use with no viewer at all. Pictures are plain `` elements unless the project gives its framework's image component: `as` on GalleryImage, `renderImage` on GalleryLightbox. For pictures that are decoration, use plain images in a grid; for one picture use aspect.

items.name: hotspots
items.title: Hotspots
items.description: Named buttons placed over a picture or a video at a point, each present only between two moments of the clip, with the same choices as a plain list for people who cannot point at the picture.

meta.when: Something in the frame can be asked about or chosen while it is on screen: an object in a scene, a place on a still, a choice in a story. Put Hotspots inside the frame (VideoPlayer, or any `relative` box over a picture) and HotspotList after it; both take the same `hotspots`. A hotspot that appears is announced, because nothing else would tell a screen-reader user it is there. For a point on a map use the map's own markers; for marks on the time bar use the scrubber's `marks`.
meta.example:
const spots = [
  { id: "kiln", x: 32, y: 55, start: 4, end: 12, label: "The kiln door" },
  { id: "shelf", x: 70, y: 30, start: 9, end: 20, label: "Drying shelf" },
];
<VideoPlayerProvider>
  <VideoPlayer aria-label="Inside the workshop">
    <VideoPlayerVideo src="/workshop.mp4" />
    <Hotspots hotspots={spots} onSelect={(spot) => openCard(spot.id)} />
    <VideoPlayerControls>…</VideoPlayerControls>
  </VideoPlayer>
  <HotspotList hotspots={spots} onSelect={(spot) => openCard(spot.id)} aria-label="In this scene" />
</VideoPlayerProvider>

items.name: input-group
items.title: Input Group
items.description: An input with a leading or trailing icon, text or button inside one shared border.

meta.when: A search box with an icon, a URL with a fixed prefix, a field with a unit or an inline action. For a plain input use input. Inside a field, wrap InputGroupInput (not the group) in FieldControl.
meta.example:
<InputGroup>
  <InputGroupAddon><Search strokeWidth={1.5} /></InputGroupAddon>
  <InputGroupInput type="search" placeholder="Search" aria-label="Search" />
</InputGroup>
<InputGroup size="sm">
  <InputGroupAddon>https://</InputGroupAddon>
  <InputGroupInput placeholder="example.com" aria-label="Website" />
  <InputGroupAddon><InputGroupButton>Check</InputGroupButton></InputGroupAddon>
</InputGroup>

items.name: input
items.title: Input
items.description: A single-line text input in three sizes, with an invalid state.

meta.when: Short free text: a name, an email, a number. Wrap it in field for a label and an error; use textarea for several lines, select for a fixed list, input-group to add an icon or a button inside the edge.
meta.example:
<Input type="email" placeholder="you@example.com" />
<Input size="sm" defaultValue="Rivier" />
<Input aria-invalid="true" aria-label="Email" defaultValue="not-an-email" />

items.name: kbd
items.title: Kbd
items.description: A key cap for showing a keyboard key or a shortcut.

meta.when: Naming a key the reader can press: in a menu item, a tooltip, a hint under a field. Wrap a combination in KbdGroup, one Kbd per key.
meta.example:
<Kbd>Esc</Kbd>
<KbdGroup>
  <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>
  <Kbd>K</Kbd>
</KbdGroup>

items.name: label
items.title: Label
items.description: The text name of a control. Clicking it focuses or toggles the control it points to.

meta.when: Every control needs one. Point it at a control with htmlFor, or wrap a checkbox, radio or switch in it so the whole row is the hit area. Inside field, use FieldLabel, which wires htmlFor for you.
meta.example:
<Label htmlFor="email">Email</Label>
<Input id="email" type="email" />
<Label><Checkbox /> Remember me</Label>

items.name: language-switcher
items.title: Language Switcher
items.description: A menu for choosing the interface language: each language under its own name in its own script, the current one marked, no flags.

meta.when: A product in more than one language: in the header or footer, and in settings. It only reports the choice (`onValueChange`): the project navigates to the translated page or stores the preference. A flag stands for a country, not a language, so none is shown. It is a menu of radio items and not a select, because choosing a language is an action that reloads or navigates: a select that changes the page as its value changes surprises keyboard and screen-reader users. For choosing a language as data in a form (a document's language) use select.
meta.example:
<LanguageSwitcher value={locale} onValueChange={(next) => router.replace(pathname, { locale: next })} label="Language" languages={["en", "fr", "ar", "ja"]} />

// With its own parts: names in the current language as a second line, and a name the project supplies
<LanguageSwitcher defaultValue="en" label="Language" displayLocale="en">
  <LanguageSwitcherTrigger />
  <LanguageSwitcherContent align="end">
    <LanguageSwitcherItem value="en" />
    <LanguageSwitcherItem value="ar" />
    <LanguageSwitcherItem value="dv" name="ދިވެހި" />
  </LanguageSwitcherContent>
</LanguageSwitcher>

items.name: lightbox
items.title: Lightbox
items.description: A full-screen viewer for a set of pictures (or any media the project renders): swipe or arrow between slides, zoom and pan, a counter, captions, thumbnails, and the picture growing out of the thumbnail that opened it.

meta.when: Looking closely at pictures that are shown small on the page: a listing's photos, a portfolio, attachments. It is a modal dialog, so focus is held inside and returns to the thumbnail of the picture shown when it closes. For a grid of thumbnails that opens it use gallery (GalleryLightbox does both). For one picture with text beside it use dialog; for a row of cards that scroll in the page use a scroll-snap row, not a lightbox. Always give it a LightboxTitle (className="sr-only" hides it) and say how many slides there are with `count`.
meta.example: {photos.map((photo, index) => ( ))} Photos {photos.map((photo, index) => ( ))}

items.name: media-row-list
items.title: Media Row List
items.description: The pictures or clips a person has added, as rows they can put in order, describe and choose a cover from: each row shows its state in words (an upload's, or one the project names), its progress or its error with pause, resume and retry, a field for its text alternative that can be required, a "cover" choice, a remove button, and room for a status line and controls of the project's own.

meta.when: After a dropzone, when the order of the files matters and each needs a description: the photos of a listing, the slides of a story, the pages of a document. It is ready-made from sortable-list (drag by the handle, lift and move with the keyboard, or the move buttons; every move is read out) and the upload rows of dropzone, and contains no upload engine: the project uploads and passes each row its state. For files whose order does not matter use the dropzone's own UploadList; to reorder things that are not files use sortable-list.

items.name: message
items.title: Message
items.description: One message in a conversation, from the person, the assistant or the system, with parts for an avatar, the words, the time and sending state, a toolbar of actions, and suggested replies.

meta.when: Inside a thread, one per message. The person's own messages sit at the end side in a bubble; the assistant's read as plain text at the start. For words that are still arriving put streaming-text inside MessageContent; for a structured piece of a reply (a plan, a form) use part-frame beside it. Not for comments under an article or a notification list: those are plain lists.
meta.example:
<Message from="user">
  <MessageBody>
    <MessageContent>Somewhere quiet for lunch on Saturday?</MessageContent>
    <MessageMeta time={sentAt} status="failed" />
  </MessageBody>
</Message>

<Message from="assistant">
  <MessageAvatar><Avatar size="sm"><AvatarFallback>AI</AvatarFallback></Avatar></MessageAvatar>
  <MessageBody>
    <MessageContent>Three places are open then.</MessageContent>
    <MessageActions aria-label="Actions for this reply">
      <MessageAction aria-label="Copy" onClick={copy}><Copy /></MessageAction>
      <MessageAction aria-label="Try again" onClick={retry}><RotateCcw /></MessageAction>
    </MessageActions>
    <MessageSuggestions aria-label="Suggested replies">
      <MessageSuggestion onClick={() => send("Only outdoors")}>Only outdoors</MessageSuggestion>
    </MessageSuggestions>
  </MessageBody>
</Message>

items.name: navbar
items.title: Navbar
items.description: A responsive site header: a brand, a row of links and a slot for actions. Below `md` the links move into a menu button that opens them in a sheet.

meta.when: The top of a site or app with up to about seven top-level links. The links are written once, as NavbarLink children, and shown in the bar or in the sheet. The sheet closes when a link in it is followed, and focus returns to the menu button. Mark the current page with `current`. With a router link, pass it through `asChild`. For navigation inside a page use tabs; for the path to a page use breadcrumb.
meta.example: Rivier} actions={} > Work Studio About

items.name: number-stepper
items.title: Number Stepper
items.description: A number with a button either side to take one away or add one, that can also be typed: a spin button.

meta.when: A small whole number that is usually changed by a step or two: people in a party, a quantity, nights. For a number where the rough position matters use slider; for a free number (a price, a year) use input with type="number". Name it with a Label (pass the same `id`) or `aria-label`.
meta.example:
<Label htmlFor="adults">Adults</Label>
<NumberStepper id="adults" defaultValue={2} min={1} max={12} />

// Controlled, with its own parts and translated button names
<NumberStepper value={nights} onValueChange={setNights} min={1} aria-label="Nights">
  <NumberStepperDecrement aria-label="One night fewer" />
  <NumberStepperInput />
  <NumberStepperIncrement aria-label="One night more" />
</NumberStepper>

items.name: pagination
items.title: Pagination
items.description: Links to the previous, next and numbered pages of a long list, with the look of buttons.

meta.when: A list or table split over pages that people may want to jump within or link to. Each page is a real link, so it works without JavaScript; with a router link, pass it through `asChild`. On the first or last page give PaginationPrevious or PaginationNext `aria-disabled="true"` and no `href`. For a feed with no natural page numbers use a "Load more" button.
meta.example:
<Pagination>
  <PaginationContent>
    <PaginationItem><PaginationPrevious href="?page=1" /></PaginationItem>
    <PaginationItem><PaginationLink href="?page=1">1</PaginationLink></PaginationItem>
    <PaginationItem><PaginationLink href="?page=2" isActive>2</PaginationLink></PaginationItem>
    <PaginationItem><PaginationEllipsis /></PaginationItem>
    <PaginationItem><PaginationLink href="?page=9">9</PaginationLink></PaginationItem>
    <PaginationItem><PaginationNext href="?page=3" /></PaginationItem>
  </PaginationContent>
</Pagination>

items.name: part-frame
items.title: Part Frame
items.description: A card for one structured piece of a conversation (a plan, a result, a form) that has a life: loading, live, saving a change, replaced by a newer one, or final.

meta.when: An assistant's reply contains something to look at or work in, not only words, and that thing changes over the conversation. The frame holds its size while it loads, says "Saving" in words while a change is on its way, shrinks to a one-line stub when a newer frame replaces it, and can open its content full screen. For a static card use card; for words use message; for a flow of steps put steps or a wizard inside it.
meta.example: Plan for Saturday // Replaced by a newer one: a stub that says so and points to it See the new plan}> Plan for Saturday …

items.name: popover
items.title: Popover
items.description: A small floating surface attached to the control that opens it.

meta.when: Extra controls or details that belong to one control: a date picker, a share box, quick settings. For a hint of a few words use tooltip; for a list of actions use dropdown-menu; for a task that must block the page use dialog.
meta.example:
Share this page

Anyone with the link can view it.

items.name: price-breakdown
items.title: Price Breakdown
items.description: What a price is made of, line by line, and the total: labels at the start, amounts in aligned figures at the end.

meta.when: A quote, a basket summary, a receipt, a booking's cost before paying. Every amount the total includes gets a line, discounts and fees too. For one figure with a label use stat; for many records in rows and columns use table.
meta.example:
<PriceBreakdown currency="EUR" locale="en-IE" announceTotal={(total) => `Total is now ${total}`}>
  <PriceLine label="2 adults" note="€46 each" amount={92} />
  <PriceLine label="Service fee" amount={6} />
  <PriceLine label="Early booking" amount={-10} discount />
  <PriceTotal label="Total" note="Taxes included" amount={88} />
</PriceBreakdown>

items.name: progress
items.title: Progress
items.description: A bar that fills as a task completes, or slides back and forth when the amount done is not known.

meta.when: A wait that can be measured: an upload, a multi-step job. Leave `value` out (or pass null) for the indeterminate state. For a short unknown wait use spinner. Always label it.
meta.example:
<Progress value={64} aria-label="Uploading" />
<Progress value={3} max={8} size="sm" aria-label="Step 3 of 8" />
<Progress aria-label="Connecting" />

items.name: provenance-label
items.title: Provenance Label
items.description: A label that stays on a picture, a video or a 3D view and says what it is (a photograph, a reconstruction, made by a model), with a popover for its sources, placed so the media's own controls can never cover it.

meta.when: A reader must not mistake what they are looking at: a reconstruction beside a photograph, a generated picture, an artist's impression, archive footage. Two placements. ProvenanceFrame puts the label in its own strip above the media, outside the media's box, where nothing the media draws can reach it: use this by default. `position` puts it over a top corner inside the media's box, above its controls and on a solid ground: use this when the label must also stay in full screen, with the label inside the element that goes full screen. The bottom edge is left to controls and captions. For the source of one fact in text use fact-row's SourceChip; for a key of classes inside a scene use certainty-legend.
meta.example:
// In its own strip above the media Drawn from the 1890 survey and two photographs. The roof is a guess.

}>Imagined reconstruction // Over a corner of a player, so it stays in full screen Imagined reconstruction …

items.name: radio-group
items.title: Radio Group
items.description: A set of radio buttons where exactly one is chosen, with arrow-key movement between them.

meta.when: Picking one of two to five options that should all be visible. For a longer list use select; for a compact row of icons or short words use toggle-group; for on or off use switch.
meta.example:
<RadioGroup defaultValue="monthly" aria-label="Billing period">
  <Label><RadioGroupItem value="monthly" /> Monthly</Label>
  <Label><RadioGroupItem value="yearly" /> Yearly</Label>
</RadioGroup>

items.name: scene-strip
items.title: Scene Strip
items.description: A row of the scenes or chapters of a clip, each with a picture, a name and a length, that scrolls sideways, marks the one that is playing and goes to a scene when it is pressed.

meta.when: Under or beside a player whose clip has named parts: chapters of a lesson, scenes of a film, steps of a recipe. It reads the time from the player it is inside (wrap the player and the strip in VideoPlayerProvider, or put it inside AudioPlayer), or from `time` and `onSeek`. For marks on the time bar itself use the scrubber's `marks`; for the spoken lines use Transcript.
